## p157 A1 — Copy-conditioned armistice-departure report fragment

**Edition context:** Armistice-departure report: the p151/p157 copy relation.

<a id="edition-cases-military-armistice-departure-copy-armistice-departure-report-the-p151p157-copy-relation"></a>



**Source comparison and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The truncated first part on p157 shares substantial ciphertext with p151 A1.
It supplies a coordinate that changes the latter's opaque `STUR3FSS` ending
to **STURZFSS** under an explicit common-copy model. The complete p157
reading below copies its missing material from p151 and prices every
disagreement. **The p157 source alone fixes 0 of 95 plaintext positions in
this conditional frame.** The copied reading is not an independent native
decryption of the 83 surviving slots.

This supplement leaves the [earlier p151 edition](151.md#edition-cases-military-nov7-fragment-and-acknowledgment-p151-a1)
and [p157 parts 2–5](#edition-cases-military-romanian-pacification-consultation) unchanged. A
further **STURZ DES** interpretation is priced separately below; two of its
letters have no surviving p157 coordinate support.

**Meaning:** The shared fragment concerns news of the departure of a German
armistice commission and an apparent effect. Its closing remains opaque in
the primary reading. BP is not expanded, and the missing predicate is not

<a id="edition-cases-military-armistice-departure-copy-sources-and-the-copy-assumption"></a>

### Sources and the copy assumption

The [p151 source](../../experiments/nov7_fragments_and_council/sources/p151_A.png)
has `LP v NKJ (6.42 p.m., November 7th)`, `KR 1215 UKS 5 TLE`, and
`1 TL RICHI-190`. It contains 189 coordinates and the visibly short `AVVG`.
Its earlier conditional edition adds D before that group to read
GEMELDETEN; that lexical assumption remains explicit here.

The [p157 first-part source](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/sources/p157_A1.png)
has `LP v NKJ (--- November 8th)`, `5 TLE` and blank `RICHI----`, beneath
the [7 November page heading](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/sources/p157_overview.png).
It preserves **83 slots: 78 coordinates and five printed dashes**. Its
four-symbol groups are `XDDV` and `XXXA`; no advertised length survives.
These headers and date layers are retained.

Two long exact coordinate runs establish the close source relation
without using German word guesses. All indices in this edition are
zero-based, and the endpoints below are inclusive.

| p151 source positions | p157 source positions | Exact length |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| 118–141 | 13–36 | 24 |
| 143–175 | 38–70 | 33 |

The reconstruction assumes the same 190-slot transposition frame as p151:
**105 absent prefix slots plus one absent coordinate in each short group**.
Thus 83 surviving slots plus 107 modeled absent slots give 190. This length
and prefix are copy assumptions, not values printed on p157.

All 25 combinations of the two local insertion boundaries are replayed.
Four share the minimum **six disagreements among 78 observed coordinates**:
`(3, 71)`, `(3, 72)`, `(4, 71)` and `(4, 72)`. Each has 72 observed agreements
with the p151 witness. The primary display uses `(3, 71)`; the other three
remain equally economical local alignments. No unique loss position or
exhaustive optimum over other total lengths is claimed.

<a id="edition-cases-military-armistice-departure-copy-the-six-disagreements-and-their-plaintext-effects"></a>

### The six disagreements and their plaintext effects

The table shows the primary `(3, 71)` alignment. Each pair combines the
listed coordinate with its other coordinate from the stated p151 frame;
these are conditional paired readings, not independently fixed p157 letters.

| p151 source | p157 source | Other p151 coordinate | p151 pair → label | Pair with p157 coordinate → label | Displayed choice and reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 114: V | 9: X | 76: V | VV → X | VX → H | p151 separator after BP; the p157 H remains an alternative. |
| 115: V | 10: X | 77: G | GV → T | GX → B | p151 T gives NACHRICHT rather than NACHRICHB. |
| 116: V | 11: X | 78: D | DV → E | DX → S | p151 E gives ABREISE rather than ABREISS. |
| 117: X | 12: V | 79: A | AX → W | AV → U | p151 W gives WAFFEN rather than UAFFEN. |
| 142: A | 37: F | 65: D | DA → 3 | DF → Z | p157 F supplies the Z in STURZFSS; the remaining FSS is retained. |
| 177: F | 71: X | 34: D | FD → C | XD → A | p151 C gives ANSCHEINEND rather than ANSAHEINEND. |

With second-group boundary 72, the last row instead compares p151 source
176 D with the same p157 source 71 X: pair DX → S versus XX → F, in
KOMMISSION/KOMMISFION. The other five rows are unchanged.

The five selected p151 coordinates are editorial choices supported by
ordinary word forms and the p151 witness; p151 is not assumed infallible.
The certificate retains **all 64 combinations** of choosing p151 or p157
at the six primary-frame conflicts. Every combination roundtrips and has
the same combined cost of six observed-coordinate changes across the two
witnesses. Coordinate cost alone does not select the displayed wording.

For p151 itself, the Z proposal costs **one observed substitution, source
142 A→F**, in addition to its already declared missing D. Its other paired
coordinate is printed on p151. The p157 coordinate therefore supports a
specific correction under the copy model; it does not independently decode
the whole closing.

<a id="edition-cases-military-armistice-departure-copy-conditional-interpretation-sturz-des"></a>

### Conditional interpretation: STURZ DES

The already edited p157 A2 begins `MINISTERIUMSHERBEIGEFUEHRT`. Joining
that continuation to a proposed STURZ DES ending would read “Sturz des
Ministeriums herbeigeführt.” This is a contextual proposal about the fall
of a ministry, with the following additional cost.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — further contextual STURZ DES proposal; two additional observed p151 substitutions, neither observed on the surviving p157 source:**

```text
OHLXBPXXNACHRICHTVONABREISEDEUTSCHERWAFFENSTILLSTANDSKOMMISSIONHATANSCHEINENDGEMELDETENSTURZDES
```

</details>

Relative to the primary STURZFSS reading, this changes p151 source
**103 X→V** for F→D and **46 X→V** for S→E. Both counterpart positions lie
inside the 105 absent p157 prefix slots. Hence the p151 total becomes
**three observed substitutions plus its one missing-slot fill**. The p157
observed cost stays five only because these two altered values occur in its
copied prefix; they are not free source support. Across both witnesses the
observed-change cost rises from six to eight.

The continuation is itself the explicitly edited p157 A2 reading, not a
literal uncorrected source. The full interpretation does not establish
which ministry fell or that the inferred event happened. In particular,
p151 A2 has a different 186-slot body from p157 A2's 200 slots: the complete
five-part telegrams are not silently equated.

## p157 A2, p157 A3, p157 A4, p157 A5 — Romanian pacification proposal and a request for consultation

<a id="edition-cases-military-romanian-pacification-consultation-romanian-pacification-proposal-and-a-request-for-consultation"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p157 A, PDF p160, is headed `LP v NKJ (--- November 8th)` and
`5 TLE`, beneath a page heading dated **7th NOVEMBER, 1918**. The
[overview](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/sources/p157_overview.png)
shows the surviving source divisions. Parts **2–5** are transcribed and
decoded below using the unchanged partial **Nov7–9** key. The incomplete
first part remains separate contextual evidence; the date difference is
not silently resolved.

The readable portions concern a proposed pacification action, a request
for a general to discuss it, and a request for early information. They do
not report that the proposed action took place. The beginning of part 2
is a continuation fragment, so the event preceding “Ministeriums
herbeigeführt” is not supplied here.

<a id="edition-cases-military-romanian-pacification-consultation-truncated-a1-source-context-excluded-from-the-four-record-count"></a>

### Truncated A1: source context, excluded from the four-record count

The [first-part crop](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/sources/p157_A1.png)
contains **83 visible slots**, including five printed dashes, under a
blank `RICHI----` length heading. Its beginning is missing, and two of the
surviving groups contain four symbols. No native full-frame decryption or
unique gap layout is asserted for this odd-length fragment.

It shares a **33-coordinate exact valid run** with the independently
transcribed [p151 A1](151.md#edition-cases-military-nov7-fragment-and-acknowledgment-p151-a1):
p151 source positions **143–175** correspond to p157 A1 positions **38–70**.
The certificate recomputes this comparison from frozen literal sources.
That is evidence of overlapping material, not proof that all source-labeled
parts on the two pages are identical. In particular p151 A2 has **186**
coordinates and a different body from p157 A2's **200**. The p151 opaque
STUR3FSS closing and the absent p157 A1 prefix remain unreconstructed.

<a id="edition-cases-military-romanian-pacification-consultation-conditional-interpretation-costs-and-reproduction"></a>

### Conditional interpretation, costs and reproduction

The four cataloged native frames contain **756 slots**, **755 valid
coordinates** and **378 plaintext positions**. Raw output fixes
**377 / 378**, edited output **378 / 378**; the exact candidate cost is
**eleven observed substitutions and one printed-mask fill**. A fixed
position can be an abbreviation or numeric label, not an understood word.
The incomplete A1's 83 slots are excluded from every total above.
No numeral assignment, key change or geometry repair is adopted.

The two bracketed display letters in `zie[h]t` and `Bukar[e]st` are absent
from the edited streams. Removing them, folding umlauts and stripping
punctuation reproduces each complete edited stream with separator X
removed. This explicit mapping is checked by the verifier. It does not
claim the missing letters were transmitted or restore them to the source.

Earlier unreviewed body candidates and the published partial key retain
their credit. The new contribution is the source-defined native frames,
visible OCR corrections, reversible repairs and complete evidence
accounting. See [inputs](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/certificates.json),
[prior candidates](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/prior_candidates.json)
and [verification instructions](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/README.md).

## p157 B1, p157 B2 — Sale of communication apparatus: p157 B1–B2

<a id="edition-cases-radio-apparatus-sale-request-sale-of-communication-apparatus-p157-b1b2"></a>



**Status:** Two readable source parts, with one final source-erased symbol still unresolved.

Source edition and repair accounting: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Published **Nov7–9** square and ranks: Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker, unchanged. Earlier unreviewed OCR-derived candidates already identified much of this apparatus-sale message. They, and their frozen p73 retrieval uses where present, are explicitly preserved; the present work provides the source edition and full repair ledger rather than a universal first-decipherment claim.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-apparatus-sale-request-meaning-and-source"></a>

### Meaning and source

The telegram tells the Nachrichtenchef that selling apparatus is advisable because of transport difficulties. It says the Romanians want to buy Siemens teleprinters and telephone apparatus, and requests permission and a sale price by radio. This is a request in the text; the edition supplies no evidence that the sale was approved or completed.

Childs printed page 157 / PDF page 160 gives `B) LP v NKJ (7.26 p.m., November 7th)`, `1400 (7) VON UKS 2 TLE`, with lengths 170 and 272. The source heading is 7 November 1918. Both native coordinate frames are preserved exactly.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-apparatus-sale-request-source-and-repair-totals"></a>

### Source and repair totals

| Part | Source slots | Printed erasures | Raw fixed positions | Edition fixed positions | Known-coordinate substitutions | Erasure fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| p157_B1 |170|4|81/85|85/85|1|4|
| p157_B2 |272|15|121/136|135/136|5|14|
| **Total** |**442**|**19**|**202/221**|**220/221**|**6**|**18**|

A fixed position means a single symbol under the stated source frame and published key. It does not mean every damaged source letter is historically certain.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-apparatus-sale-request-repairs-and-remaining-reference"></a>

### Repairs and remaining reference

`SIEMENS`, `FERNSCHREIBER` and `FERNSPRECHAPPARATE` are explicitly editorial lexical completions. Most lost letters can be filled without changing an observed coordinate. The A in `APPARATE`, however, requires **one observed-coordinate substitution in addition to its erased-coordinate fill**; the ledger does not count this as a pure erasure restoration.

Part 1 repairs raw `SC0WIERIGKE?TEN` to `SCHWIERIGKEITEN`, changing one observed coordinate and filling the missing I. This repairs a local word and does not assign H to the baseline key's digit0 elsewhere.

Part 2 also repairs raw `GENEHMIGUNGUNG` to `GENEHMIGUNGUND` at a cost of two observed coordinates. Proposed closing punctuation `ERBETENX` replaces raw `ERBETENN`, also at a cost of two observed coordinates. The source reference after it remains `KONACH18ROEMX3ANRX11023?`; its abbreviations and number labels are not expanded or reinterpreted.

The final unknown symbol has source pair `?V` at indices 40 and 245 and exact domain **DEQTUX**. It might be a separator, but this edition does not choose one. Its one printed erasure remains unfilled. No key assignment is made.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-apparatus-sale-request-reproduction-and-attribution-limits"></a>

### Reproduction and attribution limits

There are **zero added or deleted coordinates, block reorders, baseline key changes or new numeral assignments**. Every printed erasure, observed substitution and remaining plaintext domain is recorded in [the certificate](../../experiments/apparatus_sale_request/certificates.json), alongside raw and edited round trips. Global completion witnesses are consistency examples, not recovered originals.

The [input record](../../experiments/apparatus_sale_request/inputs.json) contains the literal manual rows, original headers and full crop-rendering provenance. The [experiment README](../../experiments/apparatus_sale_request/README.md) gives the default verification and optional exact PDF-pixel comparison commands.

A bounded check of the author paper and the cached complete2017 discussion found no explicit prior body identification for these particular records. Earlier machine-derived body leads remain credited, and this check is not a universal priority search.
